summary: Five columns - knowledge, harness, execution, authority and evidence - filled in one maturity level at a time, from assisted coding (L1) to governed change (L5) and parallel agents (L6).
title: Leveling up Fabric data engineering with GitHub Copilot

summary: GitHub Copilot in VS Code (or Claude Code) uses the local Fabric MCP server to create a lakehouse and land seven synthetic CSVs; reviewed notebooks build Bronze, Silver and Gold on Fabric Spark; a Direct Lake semantic model is edited with Power BI Authoring MCP; DAX checks reconcile with the Gold baseline; a two-page report is published after review.
title: HC-01: Fabric MCP + Power BI medallion lab

summary: How a request is served when services are healthy, slow or unavailable. Reads may fall back to an approved local equivalent with a visible label and reason; writes never fall back; client errors never trigger a fallback.
title: LIVE, HYBRID and OFFLINE

summary: Every agent harness shares one MCP configuration and one set of instructions. Each job uses the narrowest server: documentation tools for how, read-only tools for what is, and the approved change flow for change it. A gateway is optional.
title: MCP topology for Fabric data engineering

summary: A manufacturer's sales data lands in a Fabric lakehouse and a governed semantic model. A read-only Fabric data agent answers questions under the user's own permissions. Foundry agents reason over those answers, add allow-listed public web context, write monthly briefs for each business team, and propose data-quality fixes that a person approves and a Fabric pipeline applies upstream.
title: MFG-01: Foundry agents + Fabric for sales insights

summary: How the reference architecture is deployed for production. The application tier follows the Azure Architecture Center baseline Microsoft Foundry chat architecture (WAF ingress, private endpoints, firewall-controlled egress, managed identities, customer-owned agent state). Fabric supplies governed data through the Fabric data agent (preview, on behalf of the user). MCP tools are governed once, through an API Management-backed gateway.
title: Production deployment (aligned to the Foundry baseline)

summary: The end-to-end reference: governed business context in Microsoft Fabric, reasoning and orchestration in Microsoft Foundry, MCP as standardized capability access, Entra identity and policy as authority, a human-approved scoped writer for changes, and evidence at every hop.
title: Fabric + Foundry reference architecture
